legacy_radian_radio.prompt_mask: Given that the distance from a point $P$ to the origin is ${{radius}}$, and that $P$ makes an angle of ${{angle}}$ with the positive $x$-axis, what are the Cartesian coordinates of $P$?
legacy_radian_radio.normal_solution_mask:
We notice that the point $P$ is described using polar coordinates $(r,\theta )$, where

$$
r={{radius}},\,\theta ={{angle}}.
$$

To convert from polar coordinates to Cartesian coordinates, we use

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

First, we calculate the $x$-coordinate of $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & ={{x_sub}} \\  & ={{x_mul}} \\  & ={{x_final}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the $y$-coordinate of $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & ={{y_sub}} \\  & ={{y_mul}} \\  & ={{y_final}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $P$ are ${{cartesian}}.$
